## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Verdict | Confidence | Severity | Task Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Confirmed | High | Medium | Focused correctness bug fix |

### What Was Claimed

Issue #111 reports that npm package-selection flags are accepted by the verification command policy, but preflight checks the wrong `package.json`. The cited review finding requires validating the finding against the current integration branch, fixing the root cause, adding focused regression coverage, and re-reviewing the exact remediation head.

### What We Found

`preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` resolves the configured `cwd`, checks executable availability there, and—when `packageScriptName` recognizes a package script—reads `package.json` from that directory. The parser assumes the package-manager command is always `argv[1]` for `test`, `run`, or `run-script`.

The runtime later executes the bound argv unchanged in the resolved command cwd. Therefore package-selection options such as npm `--prefix`, `--workspace`, and `--workspaces` can select a package different from `command.cwd`; options before the npm subcommand bypass script validation entirely, and options after the subcommand leave preflight reading the configured cwd while npm selects another package. The check and the command are not equivalent.

Existing coverage proves explicit `cwd` package selection, executable preflight, and safe directory resolution, but does not cover package-selection flags or reject ambiguous command forms.

### Root Cause

The verification policy has two package selectors—`cwd` and package-manager argv—but preflight models only the former. It neither rejects package-manager package-location/workspace selectors nor parses subcommands after global options. This permits a required check to be preflighted against a manifest that the actual package manager will not use.

### Affected Files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Package script detection and manifest preflight; root-cause fix |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Focused regression coverage for rejected package-selection argv and explicit `cwd` |

### Evidence

- `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` calls `resolveVerificationCommandDirectory(..., command.cwd, ...)` and passes that directory to `assertPackageScript`.
- `packageScriptName` reads only `argv[1]` as the package-manager command and therefore does not safely model options before the command.
- `forge_verify` executes `[program, ...args]` from the same policy command without rewriting package-selection flags.
- The tracked policy and README document `cwd` as the package-selection mechanism, but no guard enforces that contract.

### History Findings

Available frozen-branch evidence shows the prior monorepo fix introduced explicit command `cwd` handling and tests. The cited source review finding (PR #110 / issue #94) specifically identifies the remaining package-selection mismatch. No unrelated changed files are present in the assigned worktree.

### Recommendation

Make `cwd` the sole package selector for statically preflighted package-manager scripts. Detect and reject supported package-location/workspace selectors in npm (and equivalent supported package managers) with the exact policy path and an instruction to set `verification.commands.<name>.cwd`. Parse only an unambiguous package script command after harmless package-manager options, or fail closed for unsupported forms. Add focused tests for selectors before and after the script command plus a valid explicit-`cwd` command.

### Related Issues

- Source review finding: PR #110, finding `correctness-001`.
- Source issue referenced by the finding: #94.
- Current remediation issue: #111.

### Decomposition Assessment

This is a bounded single-component adapter change with focused adapter tests. No decomposition or product decision is required.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Reproduce the mismatch for npm package-selection options on the frozen base.
- [ ] Reject package-selection/workspace options rather than preflighting a potentially different manifest; require `cwd` as the package selector.
- [ ] Preserve valid explicit-`cwd` package script preflight and unrelated command behavior.
- [ ] Add regression tests covering options before and after the package script command.
- [ ] Run the required `check` verification and obtain a fresh correctness/security review on the final head.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

## Builder Contract

### Objective

Ensure required package-manager verification commands are preflighted against the same package selected at execution time. The tracked command `cwd` is the sole supported package selector; package-selection argv options must fail closed instead of allowing a different `package.json` to be used at runtime.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` — package-manager option validation and preflight behavior.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` — focused regression tests for package selection and script arguments.

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change the verification policy schema, command execution, worktree boundaries, GitHub state, review policy, or unrelated adapters.
- Do not resolve package-manager selectors dynamically or execute package-manager commands during preflight.
- Do not weaken executable, package manifest, cwd, symlink, or repository containment checks.
- Do not add dependencies, credentials, fixtures containing private data, or broad parser rewrites unrelated to package selection.

### Invariants

- Required commands still use repository-relative, canonical `cwd` resolution.
- The package manifest checked by preflight is `package.json` under that canonical `cwd`.
- Any supported package-manager package-location/workspace selector in argv is rejected with the tracked command policy path and guidance to configure `cwd`.
- Arguments after the package manager's `--` delimiter remain script arguments and do not become package selectors.
- Non-package-manager commands and valid explicit-`cwd` package scripts retain existing behavior.
- No verification command is run by preflight.

### Deliverables

- A fail-closed package-selection option guard in the verification preflight adapter.
- Focused regression coverage for npm options before/after the script command, value/equal forms, workspace selectors, and a valid `--` script argument.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `A1` — Reproduce the mismatch | Regression test demonstrates package-selection options cannot override the configured package directory. |
| `A2` — Reject unsafe selectors | Adapter rejects npm `--prefix`, workspace, workspaces, include-workspace-root, and short workspace forms before manifest acceptance. |
| `A3` — Preserve explicit cwd | Existing monorepo test and a valid command with script arguments after `--` continue to pass. |
| `A4` — Keep scope bounded | Diff is restricted to the two allowed paths and existing containment/executable checks remain intact. |

### Out of Scope

- Supporting package-manager package selectors as a second trusted cwd mechanism.
- Changing command execution semantics or adding package-manager-specific runtime emulation.
- Reworking package script parsing for commands outside the cited mismatch.

## Implementation Context

### Relevant History

- The frozen branch already added `VerificationCommandPolicy.cwd` and explicit monorepo package manifest preflight.
- README policy guidance documents `cwd` as the package directory for local checks.
- Issue #111 carries the follow-up finding from PR #110 / source issue #94.

### Callers and Data Flow

- `WorkOnWorkflow` invokes `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` on the prepared frozen-base worktree before launching the writer.
- The child `forge_verify` tool later resolves the same bound command `cwd` and executes the unchanged argv with `shell: false`.
- The current mismatch is caused by package-manager argv selecting a different package than that bound cwd; rejection preserves one unambiguous selector.

### CI Surface

- `.forge/config.json` tracks one required `check` command: `npm run check`, with cwd `.`.
- Local verification is the named `check` command; GitHub CI remains the parent-owned authoritative post-PR gate.
- The regression suite runs through the repository's existing TypeScript/test check without adding a new command.

### Prior Findings

- `correctness-001` on PR #110 identifies that npm package-selection flags can cause the wrong manifest to be preflighted.
- Existing adapter tests cover explicit package cwd, executable availability, and directory containment, but not package-selection argv.

### Hazards

- Detect selectors only before the `--` delimiter so script arguments are not mistaken for npm options.
- Recognize both separate-value and `--option=value` forms, plus npm workspace aliases, while preserving the exact `verification.commands.<name>.argv` error path.
- Keep the guard static and fail closed; never infer or trust a package location supplied through argv.

## Architecture Plan

1. Add a package-manager option classifier in `verification-preflight.ts` that identifies npm package-location/workspace selectors before the script-argument delimiter. (A1, A2)
2. Invoke the classifier for required package-manager commands before package manifest validation and throw `VerificationPreflightError` instructing policy authors to set `cwd`. (A2, A4)
3. Extend the focused preflight fixture tests to cover selector forms before and after `test`, aliases/equal forms, and a valid selector-looking script argument after `--`. (A1, A3)
4. Run the required named verification, inspect the bounded diff, commit the implementation, and obtain fresh correctness/security review on the exact prepared head. (A3, A4)
